title: Cell Lysis, Two-Step Purification, and RNase Digestion
author: Clémentine elan-Forino
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bntfmejn

steps.title: Prepare RNaceIT working stock
steps.instruction: Dilute commercial RNaceIT 1:100 in water, store at 4 °C and use for all experiments; aim for an average RNA footprint length of ~30 nt.

steps.title: Maintain ice and collect aliquots
steps.instruction: Perform all steps on ice unless otherwise noted and, for troubleshooting, take three aliquots per sample at the indicated purification points (crude lysate, IgG supernatant, TEV eluate) for later Western blot analysis.

steps.title: Lyse cells with TN150 buffer
steps.instruction: Add one volume (1 mL) of TN150 lysis buffer containing protease inhibitors to each cell pellet (≈1 mL pellet per 1 L culture) and thaw rapidly.

steps.title: Mechanical disruption with beads
steps.instruction: Add 2.5 volumes of zirconia beads (~2.5 mL) to the pellet in a 15 mL Falcon tube, vortex for 1 min, place on ice for 1 min; repeat vortex‑ice cycle five more times (total six cycles).

steps.title: Add extra lysis buffer and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Add three volumes of TN150 buffer with protease inhibitors (~3 mL), shake vigorously, then centrifuge at 4 000 × g, 4 °C for 20 min.

steps.title: Clarify lysate
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant (~4.5 mL) to three 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes and spin at 16 000 × g, 4 °C for 20 min; keep tubes on ice throughout.

steps.title: Prepare IgG Sepharose beads
steps.instruction: Resuspend IgG Sepharose by gently inverting the bottle, pipette 167 µL (stock) per sample into a 15 mL tube (≈125 µL beads for a 75:25 bead:buffer ratio). Wash beads twice with 5 mL TN150 buffer + protease inhibitors, collecting beads by pulsing centrifuge at 1 000 rpm (≈210 × g) at 4 °C. Use wide‑orifice tips or cut pipette tips for efficient handling.

steps.title: Equilibrate beads after washing
steps.instruction: After the second wash, discard supernatant, add 125 µL TN150 + protease inhibitors per sample, gently resuspend, and aliquot 250 µL of this bead suspension into 15 mL tubes.

steps.title: Save crude lysate aliquot
steps.instruction: Take 5 µL of cleared lysate (crude lysate) for troubleshooting and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Bind lysate to IgG beads
steps.instruction: Mix the remaining cleared lysates with the prepared IgG Sepharose beads and rotate at 4 °C for a minimum of 2 h (can be extended overnight).

steps.title: Collect and wash bound beads
steps.instruction: Collect beads by pulsing centrifuge at 1 000 rpm, 4 °C and remove most supernatant. Wash beads twice with 10 mL TN1000 buffer and twice with 10 mL TN150 buffer; for each wash gently agitate at 4 °C for 5 min. Subsequent buffers do not contain protease inhibitors.

steps.title: Resuspend beads for TEV cleavage
steps.instruction: Resuspend beads gently in 600 µL TN150 and transfer to a 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Add TEV protease
steps.instruction: Add 20–30 units of TEV protease to the bead suspension and mix by inverting the tube.

steps.title: TEV cleavage incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate at 18 °C for 2 h with shaking, ensuring beads remain in suspension.

steps.title: Separate TEV eluate from beads
steps.instruction: Pass the mixture through a SnapCap microcentrifuge column to retain beads; spin the column at 1 000 rpm, 4 °C and collect the eluate in a 1.5 mL tube. Do not place eluate on ice.

steps.title: Store TEV eluate sample
steps.instruction: Take 25 µL of the TEV eluate, label as “TEV eluate,” and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare guanidine HCl tubes
steps.instruction: Label 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes and add 0.4 g guanidine HCl to each.

steps.title: Prepare Ni‑NTA resin
steps.instruction: Pipette 100 µL of 50 % Ni‑NTA slurry into each tube (final resin volume ≈50 µL), wash twice with 1 mL Wash Buffer I, and leave the resin suspended in ~100 µL Wash Buffer I until use.

steps.title: RNase digestion of TEV eluate
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL of the 1:100 RNaceIT dilution (0.15 U, Agilent) to 550 µL TEV eluate, mix, and incubate at 37 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Transfer RNase‑treated eluate to guanidine
steps.instruction: Immediately transfer the RNase‑treated eluate into the prepared tubes containing guanidine HCl; final volume will be ~700 µL.

steps.title: Adjust salt and imidazole concentrations
steps.instruction: Add 27 µL of 5 M NaCl (to reach 300 mM final) and 3 µL of 2.5 M pH 8.0 imidazole (to reach 10 mM final) to the eluate.

steps.title: Bind eluate to Ni‑NTA resin
steps.instruction: Remove any remaining supernatant from the washed Ni‑NTA resin, add the adjusted eluate to the resin, and incubate with gentle agitation at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Wash Ni‑NTA resin
steps.instruction: Pulse the tubes to collect the resin, discard supernatant, then wash three times with 400 µL Wash Buffer I followed by three washes with 400 µL 1× PNK buffer.

steps.title: Transfer resin to column
steps.instruction: Move the washed Ni‑NTA resin into a SnapCap microcentrifuge column for downstream processing.

steps.title: Optional Western blot controls
steps.instruction: Perform Western blots on the saved “crude lysate,” “IgG supernatant,” and “TEV eluate” samples (and any additional control aliquots) in parallel with the purification steps.

description: Take a 5 µL, supernatant aliquot for troubleshooting (“IgG supernatant”) and store at -20 °C .
